name: Apia Waterfront
tagline: Beach Road, the market and the harbour
description: The strip along the harbour holding Maketi Fou, the government buildings, the flag-tiled Immaculate Conception cathedral and most of the shops and offices. It is flat and walkable and is the whole of Samoa's urban life.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to be in the only town in the country
pros: Maketi Fou for cheap produce and food
Buses to the whole island from here

name: Vailima and the Hills
tagline: Above the town, where Stevenson lived
description: The slopes rising south of Apia, cooler and greener than the coast, holding Robert Louis Stevenson's house and his grave on Mount Vaea above it, along with the Botanical Garden and residential streets. The walk up to the tomb takes about an hour.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting cooler air and a walk from the door
pros: The Stevenson museum and Mount Vaea

name: The South Coast
tagline: Lalomanu, To Sua and the beach fales
description: The southern shore of Upolu, an hour from Apia, with Lalomanu's beach, the To Sua ocean trench and the family-run beach fales, open-sided huts on the sand let for very little. This coast took the worst of the 2009 tsunami.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the beach and the fale experience cheaply
pros: To Sua and the waterfalls nearby
cons: An hour from Apia and its services
Tsunami evacuation routes are marked for a reason

name: Savaii (the larger island, 75 km west)
tagline: The larger island, and the quieter one
description: Samoa's bigger island, reached by a ninety-minute ferry from Upolu, with lava fields from the 1905 eruptions, blowholes at Alofaaga, waterfalls and a fraction of the visitors. Village life here is more traditional than anywhere on Upolu.
bestFor: Anyone who wants Samoa with almost nobody else in it
cons: A ferry crossing from the main island
Fa'a Samoa protocols are stricter here
